spark.byteSummary:
Build reliable speed and accuracy in coding rounds using the UMPIRE loop, high-leverage DSA patterns, explicit complexity proofs, and structured dry-run verification.

Even strong engineers fail coding rounds when they start typing before clarifying constraints (empty input, duplicates, integer overflow, cycles) or get stuck debugging off-by-one errors silently.

Pattern recognition + clean invariant communication beats memorizing 500 problems—always state brute force, optimize using a core pattern, and dry-run edge cases before finishing.

concept.whyItMatters: Even strong engineers fail coding rounds when they start typing before clarifying constraints (empty input, duplicates, integer overflow, cycles) or get stuck debugging off-by-one errors silently. Following a structured loop turns coding interviews into predictable, calm problem-solving sessions.
whenToUse: Practicing high-frequency patterns: Two Pointers, Sliding Window, Monotonic Stack/Deque, Trees/Graphs, Heaps, Binary Search, and DP.
whenNotToUse: Jumping straight into coding without confirming input size $N$ (which tells you whether $O(N^2)$ passes or $O(N \log N)$ / $O(N)$ is required).
keyPoints: Use **UMPIRE**: **U**nderstand constraints & edge cases -> **M**atch to a pattern -> **P**lan & prove complexity -> **I**mplement cleanly -> **R**eview with a dry-run trace -> **E**valuate time/space.
Constraint clues: $N \le 20$ hints backtracking/bitmask DP; $N \le 10^4$ allows $O(N^2)$; $N \ge 10^5$ requires $O(N \log N)$ or $O(N)$.
Write modular helper functions (e.g., `isValid`, `dfs`, `binarySearch`) so core logic stays readable and bug-free.
Always trace 3 test cases aloud: normal case, boundary case (empty/single element), and tricky edge case (duplicates/negative/cycle).

sections.content:
## Preparation & Execution Matrix

| Input Constraint | Target Complexity | Likely Patterns |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| $N \le 20$ | $O(2^N)$ or $O(N!)$ | Backtracking, Bitmask DP |
| $N \le 2{,}000$ | $O(N^2)$ | 2D DP, Nested loops, Graph all-pairs |
| $N \le 10^5$ | $O(N \log N)$ or $O(N)$ | Sort + Two Pointers, Heap, Monotonic Deque, BFS/DFS |
| $N \ge 10^9$ | $O(\log N)$ or $O(1)$ | Binary Search on Answer, Math / Bitwise |
